P001: Single infrared image restoration; no independently acquired second modality. This is context rather than evidence for a fusion advantage.
P002: Infrared machinery diagnosis. Combining thermal regions remains image-only; vibration fusion is proposed as future work.
P003: Physical camera and audio welding classification. Split independence and controlled missing/noise evaluation are not established in the inspected postprint.
P004: Seminal evaluation foundation on model-selection bias. It does not supply an industrial fusion experiment.
P005: Transferable modality-dropout method. Training exposure and planned available-input configurations determine the robustness claim.
P006: Transferable gated intermediate fusion. Learned allocation alone does not establish calibrated modality reliability.
P007: Transferable robust multimodal classification architecture. The inspected preprint and published journal metadata refer to one work.
P008: Predictive uncertainty under dataset shift. Good in-distribution confidence does not guarantee shifted reliability.
P009: Reproducibility and reporting foundation. Documentation and code availability are distinct from independently reproduced results.
P010: The visual patch Transformer was evaluated on image recognition. The study provides no comparison of the industrial visual models evaluated here.
P011: The audio-spectrogram Transformer represents sound through spectrogram patches. The present studies include no completed audio-branch comparison.
P012: Self-supervised dilated-convolution time-series encoder. It is not a Transformer; the reported Transformer substitution performs worse.
P013: The video Transformer models interactions across space and time. The REASSEMBLE visual classifier averages frame descriptors over time.
P014: Audiovisual attention-bottleneck fusion. Transferable representation design does not establish industrial sensor-failure robustness.
P015: Multimodal benchmark and evaluation framework. Its different tasks are not independent replications of one industrial target.
P016: The missing-modality Transformer evaluation includes adverse multimodal results. For the Food dataset, the prose and tabulated unimodal result disagree.
P017: The preprint and published article on leakage in scientific evaluation give different counts of affected papers.
P018: The study evaluates pretrained time-series representations on benchmarks. Transfer of its weights to the industrial tasks considered here was not tested.
P019: The robotic assembly dataset provides native action outcomes. Its published demonstration count differs from the eligible sample for the present action-level analysis.
P020: Transferable multimodal negative-learning study. Its noise regimes and negative comparisons remain specific to the reported tasks.
P021: Physical tool images and force measurements with adaptive fusion. Post-pass image timing and incompletely reported splits limit prognostic claims.
P022: Non-industrial dynamic-fusion method. Its evidence informs fusion assumptions without constituting industrial deployment validation.
P023: Transferable constrained fusion of text with time series. It supplies negative evidence against assuming every additional modality helps.
P024: Industrial inspection using geometric prior information. RGB and geometry are distinguished from independent machine telemetry.
P025: The industrial inspection model combines visual and geometric features with language for defect reporting. Its evaluation includes task-specific supervision and measures report consistency.
P026: Train-calibrated RGB/geometry fusion includes explicit missing-3D evaluation and static/gated controls. It is not camera-plus-machine-telemetry evidence.
P027: Audio, vibration and current fusion with missing-input claims. Limited auditability excludes it from strong quantitative synthesis.
P028: Completed robotic handover outcomes with video, force/torque and gripper inputs. Added gripper input reduces one five-class accuracy result.
P029: Thermal-image and vibration fault diagnosis with single-input and noise controls. Reliability conclusions remain conditional on its protocol.
P030: PatchTST was evaluated for time-series forecasting. The PHM regression and REASSEMBLE classification experiments trained separate temporal models from scratch.
P031: Vision-language surface localization is evaluated with pixel metrics. These measure localization rather than image-level detection or numerical process sensing.
P032: Camera/audio weld-penetration attention fusion. Clean single-input and fused models all report 100% accuracy; independent-run splitting is unclear.
P033: RGB/geometry disagreement scoring. Eyecandies image AUROC decreases despite improved localization, showing metric-specific trade-offs.
P034: Space-time attention models cross-frame interactions. The core REASSEMBLE visual representation averages frame descriptors.
P035: Weakly supervised single-camera surface inspection. Internal feature fusion is not fusion of independently acquired physical modalities.
P036: Transferable counterargument on attention interpretation. Model inspection does not by itself establish a physical causal explanation.
P037: Camera/robot telemetry corruption in simulated pose regression. Overlapping temporal windows and random splitting limit physical-deployment inference.
P038: RGB/geometry consistency fusion. Its learned scalar mixing coefficient does not demonstrate sample-conditioned online reliability adaptation.
P040: Cross-validation variance theory. Overlapping training folds do not supply independent replications for a naive standard error.
P041: Validation-fitted calibration foundation. In-distribution temperature scaling is not a guarantee of reliable probabilities after shift.
P042: Single-vibration diagnosis with synthetic noise. Simulated target training and reporting inconsistencies limit transfer and field-validity claims.
P043: Distribution-shift benchmark. OOD validation access is explicit; this is not an untouched-target industrial multimodal experiment.
P044: Transferable medical fusion counterexample. Selection and evaluation share validation data; no independent final test is established.
P045: Post-pass tool photographs and acoustic emission predict wear. Strong visual and adverse multimodal comparators coexist with unresolved tool-split coverage.
P046: Microphone/accelerometer bearing fusion. Test-noise results lack an equivalent static corruption comparator; recording-disjoint splitting is unclear.
P048: Thermal-camera and vibration feature fusion. Overlapping windows, multirate pairing and separately fitted speeds restrict generalization claims.
P049: Transferable attention-interpretability critique. Attention perturbation is distinct from physical input corruption or modality dropout.
P050: Transferable unaligned language/audio/video cross-attention. Unequal feature rates are not a controlled hardware-clock offset test.
P051: Visible/infrared federated detection. Incomplete clients differ from surprise inference outage; group splits, clipped results and coefficient conflicts limit appraisal.
P052: Milling dataset with laboratory video and machine measurements. Dataset availability enables research but is not itself a learned fusion result.
P053: Audio/vibration wavelet-image cross-attention. These are transformed signals, not camera images; controlled missing/noise tests are not established.
P054: RGB/surface-normal anomaly detection. Training feature-noise regularization is distinct from a test-input degradation benchmark.
P055: Proper-scoring-rule foundation. Expected propriety does not certify finite-sample calibration or shifted sensor reliability.
P056: RGB/point-cloud local alignment preprint, version 1. Checkpoint-selection population and retraining variability remain unclear.
P057: The study uses visual symbols and language to diagnose manipulation failures. The present ViFailback experiment instead combines camera views and numerical robot observations.
P058: Transferable quality-aware weighting. Its conditional generalization-upper-bound comparison does not imply universal actual-risk superiority.
P059: Single-image object detector foundation. Executing an extracted CNN backbone does not execute the full detector or its reported inference pipeline.
